headline: Each agreement part now prints its fold before you send it.
prose: A part you write in the Galley now shows above its fold exactly as your client's copy will read, part by part as you draft. Nothing about the agreement's terms changed — only how much of the read-through happens before you send it.

headline: An invoice now says whether it arrived, opened, or bounced.
prose: Every invoice you send now carries its own delivery row: sent, delivered, opened, or bounced, beside the invoice itself. When a client says they never saw the bill, the row already has the answer.

headline: An invoice can now stand on its own printed page.
prose: Some clients still pay by check, and an invoice now prints as its own letterhead page for exactly that. Send it electronically or hand it over on paper; the ledger records the same invoice either way.

body: Invoices now say what became of the email, delivered, opened or bounced, beside each one you send.
_comment: successEvent is proposed, not yet instrumented in document-events.ts. It should fire when a delivery row is read on a visit after the invoice's own send.

body: An invoice now prints as its own letterhead page, for the clients who still pay by check.
_comment: successEvent is proposed, not yet instrumented. It should fire when a printed invoice is later recorded as paid outside Stripe.

body: Each part you write now prints above its fold exactly as your client's copy will read.
